target_customer: Grocery retailers and coffee shops buying fresh prepared food
problem: Fresh prepared food is wasteful and hard to supply with healthy options on short shelf life.
business_model: Wholesale food product sales with own production and cold chain

founders.name: James Chan
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder in the TechCrunch Aug 2022 article.

technical_complexity.rationale: Food production and cold chain logistics rather than novel technology; point of sale data analytics used.

defensibility.rationale: Fresh food brands are copyable; operations and retail relationships are the only edge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; company raised $7M in 2022 and sells at Whole Foods and Bristol Farms.

market_need_then: TechCrunch 2022 cites a $34B fresh prepared foods market; founders started selling at WeWork offices in 2018. Dated 2019 demand data not sourced.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic word brand; no source on brand effect.

pivots.to: Grocery retail such as Whole Foods and Bristol Farms
pivots.why: COVID-19 cut coffee shop orders to near zero per TechCrunch 2022.

outcome_analysis: Positive started selling healthy meals from coolers at LA WeWork offices in 2018 and reached about 70 coffee shops before COVID cut orders to near zero. It pivoted to grocery retail, reached Whole Foods and Bristol Farms and raised 7M in August 2022 with double digit monthly growth claimed. Later status is unclear, with a TechCrunch repost mentioning earlier staff cuts that are undated.
notes: Stage other because the article does not label the round (CB Insights says $7M). Founding year 2017 per YC page, 2018 per press. Only Schuyler Deerman is on the YC page; James Chan sourced from TechCrunch. No dated 2019 competitor found. Education and prior employers not found.
